drhp.business: Manaksia Steels Limited is a diversified light engineering company with a multi-location footprint, specialising in the manufacture of a wide array of metal products through advanced metal forming processes. risks.note: The global economy was affected by the US tariff shock of April 2025, which left effective tariff rates well above pre-2025 levels and heightened trade policy uncertainty, a macro backdrop that can affect input costs and export competitiveness.

The Indian rupee depreciated sharply by 9.88% during FY 2025-26 — its steepest fall since FY 2011-12 — touching H94.83 against the US dollar, which can affect the cost of imported raw materials and exports.

Foreign portfolio investors withdrew a record H1.8 Trillion during FY 2025-26, the largest outflow in 36 years, and India's market capitalisation and key indices declined during the year, reflecting a more volatile capital markets backdrop.

Continued dominance of China in the global steel market, with cost advantages and a wide product portfolio, exerts competitive pressure; aggressive pricing and dumping of steel products by China creates market distortions for domestic manufacturers.
risks.risk: China dumping and global competitive pressure

risks.note: Supply-side constraints including limited availability of domestic iron ore and coal, along with dependence on imports for key raw materials, expose the industry to external market risks; volatility in scrap prices also affects cost predictability and margins.
risks.risk: Raw material supply constraints and import dependence

risks.note: High transportation and power costs, along with elevated conversion costs, affect overall profitability; taxation and duties in India compared to global peers also impact competitiveness.
Regulatory and policy challenges, particularly related to land acquisition, are flagged as a threat to the industry.
risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risk, including land acquisition

risks.note: Increasing competition from alternative materials such as High Entropy Alloys and advanced ceramics, and the proliferation of low-cost steel produced using lower-grade inputs, intensify global competition.
risks.risk: Competition from alternative materials and low-cost steel

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The global economy was affected by the US tariff shock of April 2025, which left effective tariff rates well above pre-2025 levels and heightened trade policy uncertainty, a macro backdrop that can affect input costs and export competitiveness.
- The Indian rupee depreciated sharply by 9.88% during FY 2025-26 — its steepest fall since FY 2011-12 — touching H94.83 against the US dollar, which can affect the cost of imported raw materials and exports.
- Foreign portfolio investors withdrew a record H1.8 Trillion during FY 2025-26, the largest outflow in 36 years, and India's market capitalisation and key indices declined during the year, reflecting a more volatile capital markets backdrop.
- Continued dominance of China in the global steel market, with cost advantages and a wide product portfolio, exerts competitive pressure; aggressive pricing and dumping of steel products by China creates market distortions for domestic manufacturers.
- Supply-side constraints including limited availability of domestic iron ore and coal, along with dependence on imports for key raw materials, expose the industry to external market risks; volatility in scrap prices also affects cost predictability and margins.
- High transportation and power costs, along with elevated conversion costs, affect overall profitability; taxation and duties in India compared to global peers also impact competitiveness.
- Regulatory and policy challenges, particularly related to land acquisition, are flagged as a threat to the industry.
- Increasing competition from alternative materials such as High Entropy Alloys and advanced ceramics, and the proliferation of low-cost steel produced using lower-grade inputs, intensify global competition.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shift from commodity steel processing towards a differentiated, value-added coated steel business (galvanized, Alu-Zinc, colour-coated).
- Expand value-added coated product portfolio and raise the proportion of flat steel converted into premium branded products with higher value realisation.
- Broaden distribution footprint beyond the core Eastern India market into Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh, and continue expanding the distributor/dealer network.
- Disciplined, internally funded (equity-funded) capacity expansion rather than debt-funded growth.
